Owner decisions: T4.1 yes; publish catalog-index.json + the 12 built-in packs to the public MarceloGiazzon/NPR yes; geo first as a USER capability (customCapabilities), platform capability later; polling in sample S1. Wrote T4.1 (REG-323, fragments): new NPDevCli/npdev_relay_files.py (all-or-nothing multi-file write, backup list with previous bytes or ABSENT, undo), composed-model validation through staged folders in npdev_relay_authoring.py and npdev_relay_engine.py, apply/undo in npdev_relay_apply.py, round field backupManifestPath in the session schema, 22 tests, CHANGELOG, REG-323 note, REG-323 in ACCEPTED_R2; also fixed a failed create leaving a half-made app on Windows (read-only .git defeated rmtree). The T4.1 aiKnowledge gate then FAILED on exactly one step, portable-tooling (step 56): a drive-letter literal in my own test; fixed, that check alone passes. T4.1 is NOT committed. Measured the AI briefing bundle: 16645 chars, ZERO mentions of packs, catalog, fragments, http-connector or customCapabilities.

Because the tree changed after that run, rerun the gate on the final tree: python scripts/ai/run_digest.py -- pwsh -NoProfile -File scripts/quality/run-all-gates.ps1 -Only aiKnowledge (15-30 min, run it in the background with a Monitor on the newest *pwsh--NoProfile--File.log in D:\WorkSpace\NPDev\Build\digest-logs\, touch nothing meanwhile; the summary at the log END says PASSED or lists failures). If green: pwsh -NoProfile -File scripts/hygiene/clean-workspace-state.ps1, commit all on main naming REG-323 T4.1, git push origin main (no branch, no PR). THEN publish the 12 built-in packs to the public NPR repo (owner authorized 2026-11-11): npdev pack publish only commits when --push is given and then pushes at once, so first stage it: clone https://github.com/MarceloGiazzon/NPR to D:\WorkSpace\NPDev\Build\npr-clone, add a second remote pointing at a local bare repo, then for each D:\WorkSpace\NPDev\NPDev_General\NPDevContract\packs\<id>\pack.json run npdev pack publish <pack> <pack> --push --catalog-repo <clone> --remote <local bare remote> --repository-url https://github.com/MarceloGiazzon/NPR --tag-template {pack}-{version} (old = new for a first publish; the default v{version} collides because 9 of 12 packs are 1.0.0); also tag user-1.0.0 on the same commit as the existing v1.0.0 (pack user, so the catalog scan finds it); review git log, the file list and catalog-index.json; only then git push origin main --tags from the clone. Packs go unsigned (no owner key), consumers need --allow-unsigned. THEN the item that unblocks the owner's Uber test: make the AI briefing teach packs[] and the catalog, fragments, http-connector and customCapabilities -- the bundle is built by scripts/ai/build_core_context.py (zero mentions of these today) and the relay text is NPDevCli/relay-prompts.json, which is BENCH-MEASURED (re-measure after any prompt change; never edit platform Java while a bench run is on). After that: sample ride-hailing S1 (core, polling, geo as a user capability through customCapabilities -- first confirm a flow can hand queried driver rows to it) and S2 (payments pack + surge, no platform code; no payments pack exists among the 12 built-ins, it must be written), then T4.2 upsert; also consider a relay path for AI-authored pack.json (relay-ingest-policy.json accepts none today).
